title.narrative: Coming of Age - Alternative Rites of Passage for Young Girls

description.narrative: Despite a goverment ban of FGM in 2001, the number of girls forcibly undergoing this practice is increasing in rural communites in the project area. In Kisii and Kuria districts, 80% of women have been "cut" and 70% of girls aged 12 -16 are at risk each year. Deeply rooted customs, linked to social and economic benefits are associated with FGM. The practice harms girls' physical and psychological health: they will be taken out of school, enter into early, arranged marriages, experience consecutive, difficult pregnancies and become more vulnerable to diseases including HIV/AIDS. Lessons learnt from previous anti-FGM campaigns show that advocacy projects are useful but limited in their impact because they do not provide alternatives to the practice. Local communities feel the need to preserve traditions and customs, whilst providing the family with an opportunity to display wealth, generosity and social status. The majority of rural communities also seem unaware of the direct link between FGM and HIV/AIDS, or that the practice violates basic human rights and Kenyan law. By raising awareness of health issues, human rights and by offering alternative solutions to income for the families and traditional circumcisers, we will reduce the incidence of FGM locally.
